title: NVIDIA and Meta expand model–infrastructure collaboration
dek: A deeper Muse partnership couples model optimization with NVIDIA accelerators, networking and a $3B strategic investment.
evidence: NVIDIA/Meta joint announcement; no independently demonstrated inference TCO results
takeaway: Distinguish announced hardware/model integration from reproducible latency and total-cost improvements.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Large-scale agent serving depends on accelerators, memory, interconnects and software optimization for long conversations and tool calls.

paragraphs: Models and hardware co-evolve: Large-scale agent serving depends on accelerators, memory, interconnects and software optimization for long conversations and tool calls.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: NVIDIA and Meta plan joint performance work on Meta's Muse models for training and inference, alongside expanded Vera Rubin/Vera CPU, Spectrum-X networking and BlueField-4 adoption.
NVIDIA announced a $3B investment in Meta's equity offering; the same announcement mentions possible, not delivered, OpenShell and Sentry agent-safety collaboration.

paragraphs: Muse co-optimization: NVIDIA and Meta plan joint performance work on Meta's Muse models for training and inference, alongside expanded Vera Rubin/Vera CPU, Spectrum-X networking and BlueField-4 adoption.
Capital tie: NVIDIA announced a $3B investment in Meta's equity offering; the same announcement mentions possible, not delivered, OpenShell and Sentry agent-safety collaboration.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: The public statement describes intended hardware rollouts and joint engineering, not a controlled tokens/s, power-per-token or workload-level cost comparison.
Planned infrastructure and security integration may change before deployment; projected capacity is not current installed capacity.

paragraphs: No comparative TCO data: The public statement describes intended hardware rollouts and joint engineering, not a controlled tokens/s, power-per-token or workload-level cost comparison.
Forward-looking elements: Planned infrastructure and security integration may change before deployment; projected capacity is not current installed capacity.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Memory, networking, batching and model shape can dominate inference cost more than accelerator peak compute.
An equity commitment says little about whether agents complete work more cheaply or safely; verify on representative workloads.

paragraphs: Optimize the whole stack: Memory, networking, batching and model shape can dominate inference cost more than accelerator peak compute.
Separate investment from benchmark evidence: An equity commitment says little about whether agents complete work more cheaply or safely; verify on representative workloads.
